# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents (Claude Code reads this via the `CLAUDE.md` symlink).

## Repository

Our buyer agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (EHL Final 2026).

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `agent/` | `negotiator`: arena API client, runner, telemetry, reports, strategies (Python 3.12, uv) |
| `negotiation-arena-kit/` | git submodule: brief, API docs, data package, starter kit (read-only, do not edit) |
| `bmw_data/` | Source data, git-ignored; never commit it or copy values from it into code |

## Commands

```sh
make install                                   # submodule + uv sync
make test && make lint                         # pytest (incl. arena-sim end to end), ruff
cd agent && uv run negotiator --help           # every API call, play/run/final, report, stats
```

Arena: the key is `ARENA_API_KEY` in the root `.env`. Practice is limited to 200 sessions a day - develop on
`--set sandbox` and the local `arena-sim`; never hard-code values from the data package or replays into code.
During the Live Final the agent must not read the live feed, leaderboard or results (`NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1`
blocks them in the client).

## Benchmarks

Every benchmark run (any `negotiator run` / `play` on sandbox or practice that is used to judge a strategy) gets a
record in `agent/docs/benchmarks/<date>-<strategy>-<model>.md` (e.g. `2026-10-10-lowball-none.md`; `none` when the
strategy uses no LLM), in the same change as the code it measures. Copy the layout of an existing record:

- **Result and cost first:** score per case and mean; the deal's cost `C_deal` in EUR; what the run cost us (practice
  sessions spent, LLM tokens, wall time).
- **Strategy:** its file, a one-line description, the parameters it ran with and the commit - so a later change to
  the strategy can be told apart from the old numbers.
- **Runs:** set and cases, run ID(s) under `agent/runs/`.

A repeat on the same day with the same parameters adds a row to that record; changed parameters or a new day get a
new file. Never rewrite old numbers. One run is noise: the bots answer non-deterministically, so compare means over
at least three repetitions before drawing a conclusion.

## Rules

Read the file for the area you touch before changing it:

- [`.agents/git.md`](.agents/git.md) — commit messages (Conventional Commits), branches, pre-commit checks
- [`agent/README.md`](agent/README.md) — package architecture, telemetry layout, how to add a strategy
- [`agent/docs/benchmarks/`](agent/docs/benchmarks/) — one record per benchmark run (see Benchmarks above)

General: keep changes scoped to the request, match the surrounding code's style, run the checks above for every
area you changed, and do not commit or push unless asked.

Costs: report an LLM cost only when the provider measured it (`cost_usd` on the `llm_call` event, e.g.
`claude-code`). When it did not (OpenAI-compatible endpoints return tokens, not money), write
`APPROX-NOT-MEASURED` in place of the amount and give the token counts; never a figure computed from a
remembered price list.
# EHL Final 2026 – Tacto Negotiation Arena

Our AI buyer agent for the [Tacto Negotiation Arena](negotiation-arena-kit/README.md): it reads the case file
and the data package, negotiates by e-mail with the arena's supplier bots and closes the cheapest total deal.

```
agent/                   negotiator: API client, runner, telemetry, reports, strategies (Python 3.12, uv)
negotiation-arena-kit/   git submodule: brief, API docs, data package, starter kit (read-only)
```

## Setup

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:chessnok/EHLFinal2026.git   # or: git submodule update --init
echo "ARENA_API_KEY=<team key>" > .env                                     # git-ignored, never commit it
make install
make me                                                                     # team and practice quota
```

## Play

```sh
make sandbox                                    # the free sandbox cases against real supplier bots
cd agent && uv run negotiator play case:P05     # one practice case (200 per team per 24 h)
cd agent && uv run negotiator run --set practice --parallel 4
make stats                                      # best and mean score per case across all runs
NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1 make final                   # Live Final: waits for each wave, plays it in parallel
```

Every run writes its telemetry, transcripts and a report to `agent/runs/<run_id>/` (git-ignored). Details,
the architecture and the baseline strategy: [`agent/README.md`](agent/README.md). The rules of the game:
[`negotiation-arena-kit/brief/brief.md`](negotiation-arena-kit/brief/brief.md).

```sh
make test && make lint
```

# negotiator

Buyer agent toolkit for the [Tacto Negotiation Arena](../negotiation-arena-kit/README.md): a client for every
API endpoint, a runner that plays cases (RFQ threads in parallel, Live Final waves), full telemetry, reports and
statistics, and a baseline strategy to beat.

Python 3.12 (the arena starter kit requires it); the kit is a path dependency, so the published cost function
C and the quote-PDF parsing are exactly the arena's.

## Setup

```sh
cd agent
uv sync
# the key: ARENA_API_KEY in the repo-root .env (git-ignored); ARENA_URL defaults to https://arena.tacto.ai
uv run negotiator me
```

## Commands

| Command | What |
|---|---|
| `negotiator health` / `me` | arena up, data downloads / team, practice quota, best scores |
| `negotiator cases --set practice\|sandbox\|final` · `case <id>` | case files |
| `negotiator sessions --set …` · `session <sid>` · `thread <sid> <supplier>` · `backoffice <sid>` | our sessions, state, result + trace, threads, the supplier's back office |
| `negotiator attachment <sid> <attachment_id> -o FILE` | a supplier document |
| `negotiator board` | leaderboard (for people; refused in final mode) |
| `negotiator data` | download package v1 and the Sunday release into `agent/data/` |
| `negotiator play <case_id> [--strategy tactical\|baseline]` | play one case, with telemetry and a report |
| `negotiator run --set sandbox\|practice [--cases …] [--parallel N]` | many cases in parallel (default: every hosted case of the set) |
| `negotiator final [--parallel 10]` | the Live Final: waits for each wave, plays its cases within the cap |
| `negotiator report [run_id\|latest]` · `stats` | rebuild a run's report · best/mean score per case across all runs |
| `negotiator lessons [run_id\|latest]` | per case, worst first: score, cost blocks, the supplier's reasons per round, argument checks (also written as `lessons.md` after every run) |

Global options: `--url` (e.g. a local `arena-sim`), `--key`, `--json`, `-v`.

**Quota:** practice is 200 sessions per team per rolling 24 h; sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and `arena-sim`
are free. Develop on sandbox and the simulator, spend practice deliberately.

```sh
uv run arena-sim serve --port 8100 --data ../negotiation-arena-kit/data          # local API, scripted supplier
uv run negotiator --url http://127.0.0.1:8100 register "Team" sim                  # a simulator key
uv run negotiator --url http://127.0.0.1:8100 --key <sim key> run --set practice
```

## LLM strategy and providers

`--strategy llm` adds a model on top of the baseline: before the session opens it profiles each supplier from
its dossier (letters, notes, news, negotiation history, credit index); each round it reads the reply and picks
stance, concession, lever and arguments, and writes the e-mail text. Code still builds every term sheet from C,
inserts the checked arguments, strips IDs and figures the model wrote, and falls back to the baseline move if
the model is slow or fails.

Switch the model with one string - `--llm <provider>:<model>` or `LLM=<provider>:<model>` in `.env`:

| Spec | Protocol | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama:qwen3.6:latest` (default) | OpenAI-compatible, `http://localhost:11434/v1`, thinking off | – |

## Telemetry: `runs/<run_id>/`

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `events.jsonl` | every event: `session_opened` (opening C per supplier), `plan`, `message_sent` (sheets with C), `reply` (status, terms, C, claim results, signals, latency), `attachment`, `thread_hold`, `decision`, `conflict`, `result` |

| `sessions/<sid>/` | the documents suppliers attached (quote PDF, cost breakdown XLSX, …) |
| `metrics.json` | counters (HTTP status, claim results, supplier statuses, timeouts, deals, LLM calls, errors, tokens, fallbacks) and timings (supplier reply, decision delay after a reply, HTTP latency per endpoint, LLM latency per purpose, case duration) |
| `events.jsonl` → `llm_call`, `profile` | every model call (purpose, model, latency, tokens, output) and each supplier profile |
| `summary.json`, `report.md` | scores, C_open/C_deal/C_best/C_alt, price paths per thread, cost breakdown, claims, HTTP and timing tables |

## Architecture

```
config.py      settings from env / .env (ARENA_API_KEY, ARENA_URL, NEGOTIATOR_FINAL, …)
client.py      every endpoint; paced < 10 calls/s; safe retries with X-Move-Id; final-mode guard
telemetry.py   Recorder: events, HTTP log, metrics, transcripts, logging
data.py        data package in SQLite + facts.json; checkable Evidence (index moves, scorecard, notice, …)
profile.py     supplier traits from notes, letters, news, history (cash-short, approval ladder, hedged, …)
guards.py      hard rules before every send and accept: must-haves, alternative, valid sheets and IDs
lessons.py     lessons.md: what each case taught
session.py     Negotiation: threads, documents, costs (kit's C), send/accept/walk away, transcript
llm.py         one client for OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic APIs, switched by `provider:model`; telemetry
strategy/      Strategy protocol (prepare, decide, conclude, keepalive), baseline, llm_strategy
runner.py      play_case (one worker per thread, keepalive, deadline), play_many, play_final
report.py      summary.json, report.md, statistics across runs
cli.py         the `negotiator` command
```

A strategy only decides; `Negotiation` performs and records. To add one, implement `prepare / decide / conclude /
keepalive` (see `strategy/base.py`) and register it in `strategy/__init__.py`.

**Tactical (default):** the category goal sets the policy (anchor depth, Boulware beta, reciprocity, which
levers to trade); the supplier's profile adjusts it. Concessions are counted in C: Boulware over the rounds the
round limit and the clock leave, capped tit-for-tat by the supplier's last move (no move from it, no move from us;
a half step after two stalls; the third settles the thread). Each round sends up to three sheets of equal C: our
C-optimal terms, a trade the supplier values (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want
volume), a pure price move. Arguments are chosen by profile; irrelevant or contradicted kinds are dropped. A final
offer is probed once only when walking would cost little. The guards (`guards.py`) refuse any accept that breaks a
must-have (read on the quote PDF's standard terms; unknown counts as broken) or loses to the alternative. The tactics
are inspired by ASTRA (Kwon et al., [DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent](https://github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent)):
opponent modelling, an optimiser over the cost function, offers of equal value, tit-for-tat - no code taken.

**Baseline:** a target price from the lower of opening and current price minus an anchor per category goal
(floored at should-cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing the supplier costs C); up to three
checkable arguments (short notice vs. contract, index moves below the asked increase, weak scorecard,
should-cost, alternative quote, a cheaper rival in an RFQ); a concession schedule; three term sheets per round
(C-optimal terms, a pure price move on the supplier's terms, a shorter-payment variant at equal C); it holds a
thread on agreed / final offer / stall / close enough / last round and accepts the cheapest standing sheet that
beats the alternative.

**Experiments** (`strategy/experiments.py`): the baseline with exactly one tactic changed each - `lowball` (a deeper
anchor), `questions` (three questions per e-mail), `polite` / `shelby` (tone), `budget` (a ceiling "set by
management" that we do not cross), `trade` (no move without a move, said so). They exist to measure a tactic, not to
win; the runs are in [`docs/benchmarks/`](docs/benchmarks/).

## Tests

```sh
uv run pytest        # unit tests + end to end against a local arena-sim (started by the tests)
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.

- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,

- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

98	## 5. How a negotiation works
99	
100	- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
101	- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
102	  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
103	- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
104	  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
105	  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
106	  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
107	  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
108	- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
109	  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
110	- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
111	  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
112	  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
113	  the last round, end the thread.
114	- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.
115	
116	**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
117	you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
118	delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.
119	
120	**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
121	`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
122	`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
123	**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

125	## 6. The score: total cost in €
126	
127	Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
128	**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
129	**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
130	rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.
131	
132	| Part of C | How |
133	|---|---|
134	| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
135	| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
136	| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
137	| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
138	| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |
139	
140	**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
141	opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
142	accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
143	raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
144	some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
145	wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
146	sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.
147	
148	**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
149	reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.
150	
151	| | Terms | C |
152	|---|---|---|
153	| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
154	| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
155	| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
156	| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |
157	
158	The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
159	€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

217	  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.
218	
219	## 10. Tips
220	
221	- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
222	  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
223	- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
224	  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
225	- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
226	- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
227	- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
228	- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
229	  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
230	# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1
231	
232	The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
233	the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
234	`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
235	same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.
236	
237	**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
238	network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
239	already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
240	body may be at most 64 KB.
241	
242	Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
243	[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
244	[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
245	[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
246	[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)
247	
248	## Flow
249	
250	```
251	GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
252	GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
253	GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
254	POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
255	POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
256	GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
257	POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
258	GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
259	```

261	## Endpoints
262	
263	### Your key
264	
265	One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
266	contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
267	approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
268	(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).
269	
270	Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
271	revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
272	There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
273	organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).
274	
275	### `GET /v1/me`
276	
277	Where your team stands:
278	
279	```json
280	{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
281	 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
282	 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
283	```
284	`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
285	(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.
286	
287	### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`
288	
289	A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.
290	
291	| Set | Cases | Replay |
292	|---|---|---|
293	| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
294	| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
295	| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |
296	
297	The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
298	results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
299	names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).
300	
301	### `POST /v1/sessions`
302	
303	`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
304	from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.
305	
306	| Response field | |
307	|---|---|
308	| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
309	| `case` | the case file |
310	| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
311	| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |
312	
313	Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
314	**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
315	answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
316	starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
317	retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
318	pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.
319	
320	### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`
321	
322	Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
323	With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
324	`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
325	`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.
326	
327	A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
328	seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
329	
330	`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
331	negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
332	than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
333	you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
334	as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.
335	
336	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`
337	
338	The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
339	ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
340	"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
341	after a crash.
342	
343	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`
344	
345	The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
346	data. See [Documents](#documents).
347	
348	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`
349	
350	The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
351	(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
352	(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
353	`result` and `replay_url`.
354	
355	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`
356	
357	The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
358	same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
359	ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

361	### Lists and boards
362	
363	- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
364	- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
365	  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
366	  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
367	  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
368	  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.
369	
370	- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
371	  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
372	- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
373	  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
374	  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
375	  ```json
376	  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
377	   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
378	              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
379	              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
380	   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
381	  ```
382	  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
383	  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
384	  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
385	  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
386	  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
387	  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
388	  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
389	  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
390	  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
391	  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
392	  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
393	  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
394	  - they are for people.
395	- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
396	  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
397	  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
398	  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
399	  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
400	  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
401	  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
402	- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
403	  practice records and highlights.
404	- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
405	  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
406	  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
407	  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

409	### The structured path
410	
411	For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
412	{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
413	"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
414	{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
415	(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

417	## Messages
418	
419	| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
420	|---|---|---|
421	| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
422	| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
423	| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
424	| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
425	| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
426	| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
427	| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
428	| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
429	| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
430	| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
431	| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
432	| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |
433	
434	A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

461	
462	## What counts
463	
464	**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
465	prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.
466	
467	**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
468	in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
469	check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
470	Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
471	three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
472	are context, not checks.
473	
474	| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
475	|---|---|---|
476	| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
477	| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
478	| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
479	| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
480	| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
481	| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |
482	
483	Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
484	data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
485	true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
486	`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
487	once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
488	counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
489	supplier you cite it to.
490	
491	**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
492	and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
493	from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
494	or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
495	letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.
496	
497	**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
498	alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
499	as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
500	company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.
501	
502	## Documents
503	
504	Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.
505	
506	| Document | When | What matters |
507	|---|---|---|
508	| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
509	| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
510	| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
511	| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
512	| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |
513	
514	## Terms
515	
516	Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
517	`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
518	a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).
519	
520	| Field | Type | Meaning |
521	|---|---|---|
522	| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
523	| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
524	| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
525	| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
526	| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
527	| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
528	| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
529	| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
530	| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
531	| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
532	| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |
533	
534	## Case file
535	
536	Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
537	any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.
538	
539	| Field | |
540	|---|---|
541	| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
542	| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
543	| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
544	| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
545	| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
546	| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
547	| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
548	| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
549	| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |
550	
551	`buyer`:
552	
553	| Field | |
554	|---|---|
555	| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
556	| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
557	| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
558	| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
559	| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
560	| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
561	| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
562	| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
563	| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
564	| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
565	| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
566	| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
567	| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
568	| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |
569	
570	## Data IDs
571	
572	IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
573	column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
574	checks:
575	
576	| ID | Fields |
577	|---|---|
578	| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
579	| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
580	| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
581	| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
582	| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
583	| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
584	| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
585	| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
586	| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
587	| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |
588	
589	Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.
590	
591	## Result, trace and back office
592	
593	Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
594	end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
595	`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.
596	
597	| Field | |
598	|---|---|
599	| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
600	| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
601	| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
602	| `score` | 0-1 |
603	| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
604	| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |
605	
606	## Cost and score
607	
608	With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
609	`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:
610	
611	```
612	years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
613	committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
614	covered   = min(V, N) · years
615	pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
616	new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
617	spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
618	uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
619	C = spend
620	  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
621	  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
622	  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
623	  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
624	  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
625	  + tooling_eur
626	  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
627	  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
628	  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
629	                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
630	soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
631	```
632	
633	The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
634	expected move of the clause's series.
635	
636	**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
637	full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
638	standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
639	the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
640	(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
641	really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
642	brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
643	So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
644	You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
645	you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
646	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.
647	
648	```
649	score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
650	```
651	
652	`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
653	of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
654	lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
655	− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.
656	
657	## Live Final in waves
658	
659	The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
660	starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
661	Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
662	`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
663	wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
664	the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:
665	
666	| Field | |
667	|---|---|
668	| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
669	| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
670	| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |
671	
672	Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
673	/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
674	`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
675	deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
676	0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
677	list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
678	--set final` in the starter kit does this.
679	
680	## Time, errors and limits
681	
682	- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
683	  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
684	  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
685	  thread.
686	- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
687	  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
688	- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
689	  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.
690	
691	| Status | When |
692	|---|---|
693	| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
694	| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
695	| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
696	| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
697	| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
698	| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
699	| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |
700	
701	Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.
702
